headline: The squeeze finally reached the wreckage — Taiwan +8.4%, Nasdaq +3.4%, VIX -22% — but the 3-month bill rose 5bp and credit didn't move, so this is a short cover, not a cycle turn.
summary: Yesterday the bounce was funded by the dollar and led by defensives. Today it metastasized into the most damaged assets on the board. SPX +2.3% to 7549.9, NDX +3.4%, RUT +3.1%, DJT +3.1%, and the overnight session extended it: Nikkei +5.3% to 60456, TAIEX +8.4%, KOSPI +2.8%, Hang Seng +0.4%. The option surface finally repaired — VIX -22.3% to 19.92, VIX3M -15.2%, and VIX/VIX3M back to 0.9554 (-8.3%), out of the inversion that defined the last two weeks. MOVE -7.3% to 85.98, now -14.3% on the week. DXY -0.6% to 101.70 with USDKRW -1.3%, EURUSD +0.7%, AUDUSD +0.8%, GBPUSD +0.6%. Risk regime improves only to -13 from -15, but credit & vol jumps to -53 from -63. That gap — a violent tape, a barely-moved regime score — is the whole story.

The bill for the rally is in the front end. The 3-month bill rose 5bp to 4.24%, the 94th percentile of its year; the 2-year rose 5bp to 4.56%; the 10-year +2bp to 4.88%; the 10-year real yield +3bp to 2.66%, 76th percentile and +73bp YTD. 2s10s flattened 3bp to 32bp (22nd percentile), 3m10y 64bp and -35bp on the month. Crucially this is a bear flattening into falling inflation expectations — 5y breakevens 2.25 (16th percentile), 10y 2.22 (12th percentile), both rolling over. Markets took easing out, not growth in. The 30-year mortgage sits at 7.18%, 85th percentile, down only 10bp on the month. Every rate-sensitive equity trade that ran in October — ITB +14.0%, XHB/SPY at z=2.57, KRE/SPY +10.8% — was priced off cuts the curve just repriced away.

Oil cracked again and it is not a growth signal. Brent -6.7% to 91.72, now -12.4% on the month; WTI -5.4% to 85.93; RBOB -5.0% and -20.0% on the month at z=-1.86, 13.6% below its 200-day. But copper rose 2.5%, copper/gold +0.9% and still in the 79th percentile, so this is supply and a softer dollar, not demand destruction. Precious ripped with it: gold +1.6% to 4139, silver +2.7%, platinum +2.5%, GDX +13.6% on the week with GDX/gold turning up — yet gold/silver at 77.76 is still in the 88th percentile, +11.9% on the month. The stress print in metals has not cleared. And energy equities still have not marked: XLE closed flat, is only -2.7% on the month against Brent's -12.4%, and remains +40.6% YTD and 5.4% above its 200-day.

What did not repair: credit and the factor damage. HYG/IEF is -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over, HYG flat at the 41st percentile of its range, while SPX added 2.3% — bonds priced to loss, equities priced to relief. SKEW is still 150.3. The momentum unwind remains historic, not a dip: MTUM -20.9% 1m at z=-3.79, high-beta/low-vol -23.5% at z=-3.64, growth/value -15.5% at the 4th percentile, SOXX -29.7% at z=-3.2, QQQ/SPY at z=-3.36 and the 9th percentile. CAT is -31.2% on the month at the 3rd percentile, AVGO at the 1st, ORCL at the 1st. Brazil is still the one asset accelerating the wrong way on a down-dollar day — USDBRL 5.5034, +9.7% on the month at z=2.79 with acceleration 2.15, EWZ -24.5%, Bovespa acceleration -3.92 — while India compounds (Sensex +11.5% 1m, z=2.78, acc 2.87) on a 3.0% drop in USDINR. One day of short covering does not close a 25-point dispersion gap. Stay in the spreads.

good.text: The option surface un-inverted. VIX -22.3% to 19.92, VIX3M -15.2% to 20.85, VIX/VIX3M back to 0.9554 (-8.3%) after sitting inverted for two weeks, and MOVE -7.3% to 85.98, -14.3% on the week. Credit & vol composite improves to -53 from -63.

The squeeze reached the wreckage, not just the defensives: Nasdaq 100 +3.4% beat SPX +2.3%, Taiwan TAIEX +8.4%, Nikkei +5.3% to 60456, KOSPI +2.8%, Russell 2000 +3.1%. The most sold assets led for the first time in a month.
Dollar down a second day, -0.6% to 101.70, with EM FX leading: USDKRW -1.3%, USDINR -0.6%, USDMXN -0.6%. EURUSD +0.7%, AUDUSD +0.8%, GBPUSD +0.6% and turning up. The funding squeeze keeps paying out.
Energy disinflation is a straight consumer transfer: Brent -6.7% to 91.72 (-12.4% 1m), WTI -5.4%, RBOB -5.0% and -20.0% on the month. 10y breakevens 2.22 at the 12th percentile, 5y 2.25 at the 16th.
Copper +2.5% with copper/gold +0.9%, trend up and in the 79th percentile — the oil break is supply and dollar, not a global demand collapse. Natgas +7.0%, +12.4% on the week.

India and Mexico keep compounding on their own fundamentals: Sensex +2.2% today, +11.5% on the month at z=2.78 with acceleration 2.87; INDA +10.4% 1m; Mexico's IPC at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, +8.8% on the month.

bad.text: Rates refused to ratify the rally. 3m bill +5bp to 4.24% (94th percentile), 2y +5bp to 4.56%, 10y real yield +3bp to 2.66% (76th percentile). 2s10s flattened 3bp to 32bp, 22nd percentile. A bear flattening into collapsing breakevens is easing being priced out.

Credit still won't confirm. HYG/IEF -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over, HYG -0.1% on the day at the 41st percentile and below its 200-day, while SKEW sits at 150.3. Someone is still paying for tails into a 20 handle VIX.

The factor unwind is structural, not a dip: MTUM -20.9% 1m at z=-3.79, high-beta/low-vol -23.5% at z=-3.64, growth/value -15.5% at the 4th percentile, SOXX -29.7% at z=-3.2, QQQ/SPY at z=-3.36. One +3.4% Nasdaq day changes none of it.

Brazil is still accelerating the wrong way on a down-dollar day: USDBRL 5.5034, +9.7% on the month at z=2.79 with acceleration 2.15 and trend turning up; EWZ -24.5% 1m at z=-3.25; Bovespa acceleration -3.92 despite +2.2% today.

Energy equities have not marked to the crude break: XLE flat on the day, only -2.7% on the month against Brent -12.4%, still +40.6% YTD and 5.4% above its 200-day. XOP -7.7% 1m, OIH -13.5% on the week and already 10.5% below its 200-day.

The industrial/capex complex is in outright liquidation: CAT -31.2% on the month at z=-3.52 and the 3rd percentile, ETN -20.8% at z=-2.92, GEV -22.3%, GRID -14.2%, industrials/utilities -7.5% at z=-1.75.

trades.name: Energy equities mark to $92 Brent
trades.line: Short XLE/XOP: energy hasn't marked to $92 Brent
trades.expr: Short XLE outright, or buy Jan XLE 58 puts; higher-beta version is short XOP against long XOM to keep the integrated hedge.
trades.thesis: Brent has fallen 12.4% in a month and gasoline 20.0%, yet the only sector that worked all year is down 2.7% on the month and still 5.4% above its 200-day. Earnings revisions follow the strip, not the tape, and the group is the single most crowded long left in US equities.
trades.trigger: Brent -6.7% to 91.72 and WTI -5.4% to 85.93 today, RBOB -5.0% at z=-1.86 and 13.6% below its 200-day, while XLE closed flat (-0.0%) and XOP -0.2%. USDCAD unchanged on a -0.6% dollar day is the corroborating tell.
trades.stop: Brent reclaiming $100 or XLE closing above 64; also stop if copper rolls over hard, signalling the oil break is demand-led and equities already discount it.

trades.name: Buy vol back at a 19 handle
trades.line: Buy Dec VIX call spreads with VIX back down at 19.9
trades.expr: Dec VIX 24/32 call spreads for 1-1.5 vols, or an SPX Dec 7200/6800 put spread financed by selling the 7900 call.
trades.thesis: The term structure just normalized at exactly the moment the underlying stress indicators did not. Buying convexity is cheapest the day after a 22% vol crush, and the setup — credit lagging, a bid for tails, front-end yields rising — is the classic second-leg configuration.
trades.trigger: VIX -22.3% in one session to 19.92 (37th percentile) and VIX/VIX3M back to 0.9554 from inverted, yet SKEW is still 150.3 and HYG/IEF is at z=-2.06 and rolling over. The 3m bill and 2y both rose 5bp on a +2.3% SPX day.
trades.stop: VIX holding below 17 for a week with HYG/IEF turning up and the 2-year back under 4.40%.

trades.name: Fade the AI-power squeeze
trades.line: Fade the AI-power squeeze: short VST, GEV, NLR
trades.expr: Short VST and GEV outright, NLR as the basket leg, roughly a third each; use Jan VST puts if borrow is expensive.
trades.thesis: The power/nuclear/grid complex is the purest leveraged bet on AI capex and it is being de-rated, not corrected. A one-day 10% move in a stock that is 18% below its 200-day and in the 16th percentile of its year is short covering, and it hands you the re-entry.
trades.trigger: VST +10.6% in a day but -25.1% on the month at z=-2.18 and 18.1% below its 200-day; CEG +4.3% but at the 10th percentile; NLR +4.4% and URA +4.4% off 4th-percentile lows; GRID -14.2% 1m at z=-2.57; GEV -22.3% 1m. ETN -20.8% and CAT -31.2% say the capex impulse is turning, not pausing.
trades.stop: VST back above 150 or NLR reclaiming its 200-day; also stop if SMH takes out its October highs and the whole AI chain re-rates.

trades.name: Long India vs short Brazil
trades.line: Long India vs short Brazil: INDA / EWZ
trades.expr: Buy INDA, short EWZ at equal dollar notional. Institutional version: Nifty futures long vs EWZ puts or BRL forwards short.
trades.thesis: Two EM stories heading in opposite directions with opposite currency funding. India is being bought with a strengthening rupee; Brazil is being sold with a currency in free fall. On a day when the dollar fell 0.6%, BRL was the only major that did not participate — that is idiosyncratic, and idiosyncratic trends persist.
trades.trigger: Sensex +11.5% on the month at z=2.78 with acceleration 2.87, INDA +10.4%, funded by USDINR -3.0% at z=-2.93. Against that, USDBRL +9.7% on the month at z=2.79 with trend turning up and acceleration 2.15, EWZ -24.5% at z=-3.25, Bovespa acceleration -3.92.
trades.stop: USDBRL back under 5.20, or INDA underperforming EEM by 5% from entry.

trades.name: Short the gold/silver ratio
trades.line: Long silver vs gold: short the 77.8 ratio
trades.expr: Long SLV against short GLD at 1:1 notional, or long March silver futures vs short gold futures on equal dollar value.
trades.thesis: Gold/silver at 77.8 is a stress reading, not a fundamental one — it blew out 11.9% in a month while the dollar was squeezing everyone. With the dollar now falling two sessions running and industrial metals bid, the ratio mean-reverts faster than either leg moves alone.
trades.trigger: AU_AG 77.76 at the 88th percentile and z=1.76, but silver +2.7% today, platinum +2.5%, copper +2.5% and DXY -0.6%. Silver is 23.5% below its 200-day at the 6th percentile of its year; GDX +13.6% on the week with GDX/gold turning up at acceleration 1.11.
trades.stop: Ratio above 83, or silver losing 48 — that would mean the liquidation phase is not over.

trades.name: Credit never confirmed the bounce
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: credit never confirmed
trades.expr: Short HYG against long IEF, roughly 1:1 notional; or buy HYG Jan 76 puts outright for defined risk.
trades.thesis: Equities have now rallied two sessions and high yield has gone nowhere. Every genuine turn in the last decade has been led, not lagged, by credit. Until HYG/IEF stops making lower lows, the equity bounce is a positioning event.
trades.trigger: HYG/IEF -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over while SPX added 2.3%; HYG -0.1% on the day at the 41st percentile and 0.8% below its 200-day. LQD is also below its 200-day. The ratio is the single worst z-score in the credit block.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF closing back above its 200-day, or the ratio z-score crossing zero.

trades.name: Housing priced cuts that got repriced
trades.line: Short ITB: housing priced cuts the front end took back
trades.expr: Short ITB or buy Jan ITB puts; market-neutral version pairs it against long XLV, which is +15.7% relative to the S&P over a month and still trending up.
trades.thesis: Homebuilders rallied 14% in a month on an easing path that the curve just unwound. Mortgage rates have not actually fallen — 7.18%, 85th percentile, down 10bp in a month — so the move is multiple expansion against unchanged affordability.
trades.trigger: ITB +14.0% on the month at z=1.68 with acceleration 2.07, XHB/SPY at z=2.57, yet the 2-year backed up 5bp to 4.56% and the 3m bill to 4.24% at the 94th percentile, and 2s10s flattened to 32bp. DHI already -3.4% on the last print, XHB -1.5%.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage under 6.90% or the 2-year under 4.35% — that would validate the easing bet.
